explain: Arrival order does not determine authoritative freshness. A late result computed from an older revision must not replace the newer state.
steps: Keep the current source revision with published state. || Accept updates only when their source revision is at least current.
name: revision-publication

explain: A connection can end while its task continues. Connection, session, and durable task identities must not be conflated during recovery.
steps: Close the connection without modifying durable task state. || Inspect the task through its own identity after the connection is gone.
name: independent-lifetimes

explain: Replace obsolete pending state refreshes while preserving distinct business commands. Coalescing is safe only for events whose meaning is the latest state.
steps: Retain the highest revision for each document. || Keep every unique command identity in a separate collection.
name: coalesce-state

explain: A live-system demonstration needs failures and recovery as well as a fast happy path. Required evidence is checked by scenario identity.
steps: Declare reconnect, correction, overload, and restart scenarios. || Report what has not yet been demonstrated.
name: live-recovery-proof

explain: Queue age and freshness lag can reveal user impact even when a connection heartbeat is healthy. Their meanings are recorded separately.
steps: Record source revision and served revision. || Calculate lag independently from transport liveness.
name: live-signals

explain: A source-linked reasoning fixture. JSON parsing checks representation only; reproduce the actual mechanism with the chapter reference.
steps: Inspect the declared input and required invariant. || Trace the chapter mechanism and reproduce the stated case. || Change the stated assumption and defend the result.
expect: Reasoning input only; no program result is claimed. Reproduce the scenario using the chapter’s runnable reference.
limit: A JSON case is parsed for representation integrity only, not executed as a proof of its semantic claim.
